short.q: A cyclist travels 300 m in 50 s, stops for 20 s, then travels 180 m in 30 s. Calculate her average speed for the whole journey.
short.model: Total distance = 480 m, total time = 100 s, so average speed = 4.8 m/s.

short.q: A distance–time graph shows a straight line sloping upwards, then a horizontal line. Describe the motion.
short.model: The object first moves at constant speed, then stops (at rest).

short.q: State the difference between speed and velocity.
short.model: Speed is distance per unit time and has no direction (scalar); velocity is speed in a given direction (vector).

short.q: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 24 m/s in 8.0 s. Calculate its acceleration and the distance it travels in this time.
short.model: a = 24 ÷ 8.0 = 3.0 m/s². Distance = area = ½ × 8.0 × 24 = 96 m.

short.q: Explain why a stone sinking in thick oil reaches a constant speed.
short.model: At first weight is the only force so it accelerates. Drag increases with speed, reducing the resultant force, until drag equals weight; the resultant force is then zero so speed is constant.
points: drag = weight so resultant force is zero
